successors.note: 1527-1528: the bishop 'sold his territories, and thus his secular authority, to Holy Roman Emperor Charles V' and the principality 'was conquered by Habsburg troops in 1528'; the southern Oversticht became the Lordship of Overijssel and the south-western Nedersticht around Utrecht the Lordship of Utrecht (the Habsburg Netherlands). The Drenthe and Groningen parts become the County of Drenthe and the Lordship of Groningen after 1536.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Utrecht row; its Holy Roman Empire shape draws the land as imperial). In 1024 the territory 'was divided into the Nedersticht (Lower Sticht, roughly corresponding to the present day province of Utrecht)' and the 'Oversticht (Upper Sticht, encompassing the present-day provinces of Overijssel, Drenthe, and part of Groningen)'. The Battle of Ane page dates the Oversticht to 'the mid-11th century' (imperial fiefs). The page gives no area; the provinces are the modern units and the Groningen circle is the researcher's.

ledger.note: 1024: the bishops become princes. 'In 1024 the bishops were made Princes of the Holy Roman Empire and the new Prince-Bishopric of Utrecht was formed'; the territory was 'Sticht Utrecht or Het Sticht', the Nedersticht (roughly the present province of Utrecht) and the Oversticht (Overijssel, Drenthe and part of Groningen). The Battle of Ane page has the bishops hold Groningen, Overijssel and Drenthe 'as imperial fiefs' from the mid-11th century, so the Oversticht may be later than 1024.

ledger.counterpart: Leffard and Ludolf (Groningen and Drenthe fiefs)
ledger.note: 1141: 'Hartbert van Bierum, the Bishop of Utrecht gave Groningen and Drenthe as fiefdoms' to Leffard and Ludolf; their heirs Egbert of Groningen and Rudolf II of Coevorden later fought each other and the bishop's troops.

28 July 1227: Battle of Ane. 'The Drenths managed to beat the Bishop's forces, and killed most of it including the Bishop Otto II of Lippe', near Ane in Overijssel, where the bishop had gone 'to the valley of the Overijsselse Vecht' to bring Drenthe to order.

1233: 'Wilbrand's successor Otto III van Holland succeeded in suppressing the rebellion by mustering a large army' after the Friso-Drentic War of 1231-1233, which the Drenths 'initially won'; as penance they had to build the monastery Sancta Maria de Campe near Coevorden.

wars.name: Battle of Ane and the Friso-Drentic War
wars.outcome: The Drenths beat the bishop's army at Ane on 28 July 1227 and killed Otto II of Lippe; Wilbrand van Oldenburg then roused the Frisians against them (Friso-Drentic War 1231-1233, initially won by the Drenths); in 1233 Otto III van Holland suppressed the rebellion.

notes: Four pages opened. The pages give no area or border: the Nedersticht is drawn as the modern province of Utrecht, Overijssel and Drenthe as modern provinces, and 'part of Groningen' as a circle. Not settled: when the Oversticht came to the bishops (1024 on the main page, 'mid-11th century' on the Battle of Ane page), who held Groningen after 1141, the County of Zutphen (a fief of the bishop, 'Utrecht included County of Zutphen (until 1182)' in a footnote; the Zutphen page gives no grant date, so it is not drawn), the 1512 against 1548 Burgundian Circle entry, and the end year of Henry of the Palatinate (1528 against 1529). A footnote on the main page also lists the Duchy of Bouillon in 1096, the county of Loon in 1366 and the county of Horne in 1568; these match the Liège page and are not Utrecht events, so they are not used. The Guelders Wars have infobox dates only.
